WHAT CHANGED vs v1: Pro reframes the product as loss-avoidance ('don't lose this job because of a miss or a mistake') — a survival framing that is more vivid than 'alerts' (a missed DV slot or rejected form can cost a year; age cut-offs make some losses permanent). Persistent reminders and the what-you-need card strengthen control. Family mode adds a thin belonging thread (parent involvement is culturally real in Indian govt-job pursuit) but does not lift belonging above 2 because it is notification-sharing, not community. WHY SCORES DID NOT RISE: the survival pain is real but episodic and low-probability per user — most applicants never miss a DV slot (only ~5% of SSC CGL applicants even reach Tier 2), boards SMS/email registered candidates, and Telegram/YouTube broadcast every admit card. Desire for the OUTCOME is strong; desire for THIS PRODUCT stays moderate. Weighted strength = 4x0.3 + 4x0.3 + 3x0.2 + 2x0.1 + 1x0.1 = 3.3 -> moderate (identical to v1; Form Pakka was argued slightly higher on survival because its pain — rejection — is more frequent than lifecycle misses). Virality medium: aspirants forward notifications heavily; an 'eligible for X, last date Y' card could ride it; family mode creates a second recipient but usually via WhatsApp, not an install.
